# Use-Case Guidance

Canonical source: https://review.docs.netapp.com/us-en/content-standards/use-cases/use-cases.html

Use-case content explains the user's motivation and the business problem that a documented capability helps solve. It answers why, what, and how at a high level; this skill writes a compact imperative purpose statement, not the procedural portion or a full end-to-end workflow.

Validate each draft against these questions:

1. Who is the user or operational role?
2. What outcome does the user need?
3. Why does that outcome matter to their business or operations?
4. Which documented capability supports that outcome?

Feature-based content says what a capability does. Task-based content says how to perform an action. User-focused use-case examples provide motivation and context without duplicating either type of content.

Use this writing pattern:

`<Imperative verb> <concrete problem> before or so that <documented operational consequence>.`

Prefer one sentence of 12 to 25 words. Begin with an imperative verb, use one concrete operational consequence, and mention the capability only when needed for clarity. Do not rephrase the page lead, summarize several capabilities, or add an unsupported result.
